definitions.explanation: A person who is sent to run errands or do minor tasks for someone else. Often carries a negative nuance of being treated as a subordinate.
The act of going somewhere to carry out small tasks on behalf of someone else.

examples.japanese: ⟦{先輩|せんぱい}→先輩：01451_senpai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{使|つか}い{走|ばし}り⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦させられた→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I was made to run errands for my senior.
I don't want to be stuck playing the gofer forever.

examples.japanese: ⟦{新人|しんじん}→新人：02500_shinjin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ころ→〜ころ：03091_koro⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{毎日|まいにち}→毎日：00729_mainichi⟧{使|つか}い{走|ばし}り⟦ばかり→〜ばかり：02006_bakari⟧だった。
examples.english: When I was new, all I did every day was run errands.

examples.japanese: ⟦ちょっと→ちょっと：00595_chotto⟧{使|つか}い{走|ばし}り⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{頼|たの}まれた→頼む：01104_tanomu⟧。
examples.english: I was asked to run a quick errand.

examples.japanese: {使|つか}い{走|ばし}り⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}って→行く：00119_iku⟧くる。
examples.english: I'm going to run an errand.

examples.japanese: ⟦{買|か}い{物|もの}→買い物：00853_kaimono⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{使|つか}い{走|ばし}り⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{一日|いちにち}→一日：00942_ichinichi⟧⟦{終|お}わった→終わる：00567_owaru⟧。
examples.english: The whole day was spent running shopping errands.

notes:
USAGE:
When referring to a person (sense 1), it often implies being treated as a lowly subordinate. Common in workplace and school hierarchies. Also written as {使|つか}いっ{走|ぱし}り with a geminate consonant in casual speech.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {使|つか}い{走|ばし}り⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦させる→する：00392_suru⟧ (to make someone run errands)
- {使|つか}い{走|ばし}り⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦させられる→する：00392_suru⟧ (to be made to run errands)
- {使|つか}い{走|ばし}り⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧ (to go on an errand)
